newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends lower and near major support.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends lower and near major support.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed an active session weaker, but trade buying managed to carry the spot-March contract out from under major support, where it traded in early dealings, market sources said.
Light fund selling began when the March contract reached the day's high of 10.84. The buying dried up and the selling accelerated around the previous low of 10.69.
Nearby support remains at 10.60 but longer term support was pegged at 10.55. Resistance was seen at 10.80.
One broker suggested players had been long in anticipation of Hurricane Lili. But it is too soon to gauge damage to Cuba's sugar crop, which accounts for less than five percent of world output.
"No one is very concerned about it," the broker said."
The spot-March contract settled down 0.13 to 10.64, ranged 10.84 to 10.55. The back months closed 0.11 to 0.02 lower.
Volume was estimated to have reached a brisk 21,983 lots.
Most market sources see prices heading even lower as demand is not likely to keep pace with supply.

International Sugar Organization (ISO) today put world sugar production at 123.8 million tonnes raw value in 1996/97, market sources said. ISO said a surplus of 2.5 million tonnes could push prices towards 10.00 cents per lb.
